items.headline: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
items.blurb: Hopes for an agreement on tackling climate change collapsed after a row about mentioning fossil fuels
items.text: Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey. Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history. But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming. Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures. The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed". items.blurb: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the…
items.text: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press. Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war. items.headline: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
items.blurb: The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.
items.text: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially come to an end after countries failed to come to a consensus on a new deal. The European Union and some other countries rejected a fourth draft agreement over its failure to mention a need to phase out fossil fuels, the largest driver of global climate change. An EU representative accuses some oil states of hijacking talks, as Russia defends opposing the inclusion of such a commitment and levels direct criticism at the EU in its speech. The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end. BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard reports from Antalya, in Turkey.

items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.headline: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
items.blurb: Libya's eastern government says the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.
items.text: An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said. The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government. The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment. Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said. Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port. items.headline: South Korea’s stock market tumbles as AI bubble fears mount
items.blurb: The Kospi falls more than 3 percent as markets across the region brace for losses.
items.text: South Korea’s stock market has opened to sharp losses as markets across Asia brace for volatility amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom. The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) fell as much as 3.7 percent in early trading on Monday, continuing Friday’s tech-led sell-off across the Asia-Pacific region and in the United States. The Kospi’s retreat came as investors anticipated volatile trading across the region upon the opening of key markets in Taiwan, China and Hong Kong later on Monday morning. On Friday, the Kospi closed down 5.2 percent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 and Taiwan’s Taiex tumbled 5.1 percent and 6.2 percent, respectively. On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P500 closed 3.7 percent lower for its seventh straight loss, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3 percent to erase all of its gains for 2026. Investors have long been concerned that tech firms may not be able to sustain the multi-trillion-dollar investments they have poured into infrastructure to power AI. items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.blurb: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from the scene of a collapsed residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region.
items.text: Several bodies have been recovered from the site of a residential building that was hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Services said. The attack early on Sunday morning in the village of Dymer killed six people, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said. Six people were injured, while others are still missing. Continued warnings of further drone threats near the site have hampered efforts, the service added, but some people were successfully evacuated earlier in the day. "We are living a nightmare... only God knows when it will end," one woman told the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, who's reporting from Ukraine's Kyiv region.

items.text: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh . “Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons. Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language. “Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the fundamental question at that time should have been the protection of people and the creation of a democratic environment. Instead, the leadership surrendered to religious fundamentalism, he said. In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water". A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis. "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said. Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added. The department further directed schools to publish the detailed break-up of the 100-point admission criteria on their respective websites. items.text: After the final electoral rolls from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were published, several people whose names had been deleted challenged their exclusion. They argued that they were left out despite having completed the entire process, including attending hearings and submitting the required documents. More than 350 appeals have been filed across Karnataka so far. The Deputy Commissioner or District Election Officer (DEO) serves as the first appellate authority in the SIR, while the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) is the second and final appellate authority if the first-stage response is unsatisfactory. According to the CEO’s office, all appeals received so far remain pending or have been disposed of at the first appellate stage. The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who have challenged their deletion. While some said officials advised them to withdraw their appeals and apply afresh through Form 6, others said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal. This has enabled Flipkart Wholesale to improve fleet productivity without compromising delivery efficiency, reducing vehicle idle time by 10 per cent, Far Eye said in a statement. The improvements come from digitising and connecting dispatch, routing, compliance and payment collection processes across a network comprising 26 stores and one cross-dock, it said. Flipkart Wholesale's network processes more than 200,000 orders and about 195,000 vehicle assignments a month. The platform said it now supports the movement of goods across this network through a unified digital workflow, replacing largely manual and fragmented dispatch processes. Far Eye said it also brought optimisation to match vehicle deployment to operational need, along with automated e-way bill generation, thus removing manual work from a compliance-heavy step. items.text: US Treasury futures declined as demand for havens waned on signs that the recent selloff in equities may be drawing some buyers back. Futures on 10-year Treasury notes fell 9/32 to 106 18/32 in early trading in Asia on Monday, the equivalent of a roughly four-basis-point advance. There’s no cash trading in the Asia session due to a public holiday in Japan. The move comes as US equity-index futures gained following a rout that was sparked by an unwinding of the artificial intelligence trade. Authorities across Asia stepped up efforts to stem the deepening stock-market rout, with measures including widening curbs on short selling and an easing of margin requirements. “US equity futures have rallied in Asia time this morning and this improvement in sentiment seems to be the driver of US Treasury weakness,” said Andrew Ticehurst, a senior strategist at Nomura in Sydney. The drop in Treasury futures underscore how bonds are once again moving in the opposite direction to equities as investors debate if stocks are primed for a rebound. items.blurb: Chris O'Shea says the number of people unable or unwilling to pay their energy bills will increase when prices jump in the new year.
items.text: The boss of British Gas owner Centrica says he is "hugely concerned" about the impact the expected jump in energy bills in January will have on consumers. Chris O'Shea told the BBC he thought the number of people unable or unwilling to pay their energy bills would rise when prices go up in the new year. The new energy price cap to take effect from January will be announced on Wednesday and consultancy Cornwall Insight has forecast it will jump by £443 a year for a typical household. The government has said some households will get £100 to help with energy bills, but Citizens Advice said it was a "drop in the ocean" while one pressure group called for action on "inflated energy firm profits". Speaking to the Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, O'Shea said the predictions for a "substantial increase" in bills from January were "materially correct", adding that the first quarter of the year was the time when most energy was consumed. items.blurb: It seems India’s fintech investors may have counted their chickens too early. The timeline for the much-anticipated merchant discount rate…
items.text: With MDR implementation potentially delayed until 2027, fintech stocks face an earnings reality check, while uncertainty over UPI monetisation casts a shadow on upcoming IPO valuations It seems India’s fintech investors may have counted their chickens too early. The timeline for the much-anticipated merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions has been deferred further down the calendar . The proposed monetisation of India’s UPI ecosystem was expected to be a post-Diwali bonus for digital payment companies, with a promise of a much-needed revenue stream after years of operating in a largely zero-MDR environment. However, uncertainty around the rollout is now weighing on investor sentiment, with shares of Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik enduring a sharp correction. Consequently, the optimism that once buoyed fintech stocks is fading. As of Friday (November 20), Paytm parent One 97 Communications had already fallen as much as 10.8% over the past week, while One MobiKwik Systems declined 6.6% and Pine Labs dropped 9.4% on the BSE. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.text: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity. Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name ) could be that measurement. items.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. items.headline: Sarvam’s Token Factory Raises India’s AI Inference Stakes
items.blurb: Sarvam AI’s latest announcement of its Token Factory has brought a new layer of India’s artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem…
items.text: Sarvam AI's Token Factory launch has brought India's emerging inference-as-a-service market into focus, with L&T, E2E Networks' Jarvislabs, Utho Labs and Mirror Security also building offerings around token-based AI infrastructure. Token factories allow developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through APIs and pay for the tokens they consume, without having to manage GPU infrastructure or model deployment themselves. As AI adoption drives demand for inference, Indian infrastructure players are looking to move beyond GPU rentals and monetise computing capacity through managed services, with an opportunity to serve both domestic and global workloads. Sarvam AI’s latest announcement of its Token Factory has brought a new layer of India’s artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem into focus. The Bengaluru-based startup on November 16 launched a commercial platform that allows developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through its computing infrastructure. The launch comes as Indian companies look to capitalise on the growing demand for AI inference, the process through which trained models generate responses to user prompts.
